nfl.oneThing: The Giants have benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading for J.J. McCarthy, who will make his first career start against the Texans in Week 7.

headlines.title: Giants turn to J.J. McCarthy after benching Winston
headlines.summary: The Giants benched Winston after a rough game in which he went 14-of-26 for 152 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, while New York trailed 34-10 in the fourth quarter. McCarthy came in and went 11-of-21 for 243 yards and a touchdown, giving the Giants a chance at a comeback. He becomes the third Giants starter this season, after Jaxson Dart, who tore the MCL and meniscus in his left knee in Week 2 and is out for the season. Winston started the past four games, going 2-1-1, and says he accepts the backup role.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Giants are 3-2-1 and the NFC's fourth seed, so how McCarthy performs over his first starts will shape their hold on a playoff spot.

headlines.title: Lamar Jackson back on the practice field, but still unclear for the Bengals
headlines.summary: Jackson returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since spraining his left ankle, 17 days ago. He was listed as a limited participant, walked with a limp and took part in some team drills, according to coach Jesse Minter. Rashod Bateman, who left last Sunday's loss to the Browns with a shoulder injury, was also limited. Centre Cam Jurgens was a full participant for the first time since joining the Ravens.
headlines.whyItMatters: Baltimore is 4-2 and currently outside the seven AFC playoff seeds, so Jackson's health matters for the race.

headlines.title: Cowboys still in the NFC East race at 2-4
headlines.summary: Dallas is 2-4 after six weeks, but all four NFC East teams failed to win for the second week in a row, leaving the division open. Yahoo's column argues the Cowboys should stick with coach Brian Schottenheimer despite questions about his decisions. It also suggests another big trade could come before the November 10 deadline. CeeDee Lamb's 577 receiving yards rank third in the league.
headlines.whyItMatters: No NFC East team is pulling away, so the Cowboys are still very much alive, and a move before the deadline could decide how seriously they chase the division.

nba.oneThing: The Warriors have begun exploring trades for Kristaps Porzingis, who is out indefinitely with recurring symptoms from POTS, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

headlines.title: Thunder beat Spurs 116–104 in the season opener
headlines.summary: Oklahoma City beat San Antonio 116–104 on opening night in San Antonio. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 32 with six rebounds, four assists and three blocks, and Jared McCain hit six threes for 20 points. Victor Wembanyama had 12 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks, but he missed his first 12 shots. De'Aaron Fox was given a flagrant foul on Chet Holmgren, and tensions flared into a scuffle.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Thunder start 1-0 and the Spurs are 0-1 and 15th in the West, and the rivalry has started with plenty of bad blood.

headlines.title: Warriors explore trades for Porzingis amid health concerns
headlines.summary: The Warriors have begun exploring trade options for Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely with a private health issue. The club said it won't comment on trade speculation or his health. Porzingis was diagnosed with POTS in 2025, and is seriously contemplating his future in basketball. He signed a two-year, $40 million extension in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million second-season salary is guaranteed. Golden State is hard-capped at the second apron, so it can't take back more salary than it sends out.
headlines.whyItMatters: He was set to be the projected starting centre alongside Draymond Green and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, so losing him would reshape the frontcourt, and a trade this early in the season will be hard to find.

headlines.title: 76ers beat Knicks 106–100 on ring night
headlines.summary: Philadelphia spoiled the Knicks' ring night at Madison Square Garden. Tyrese Maxey scored 28 with five assists, three blocks and three steals, and Jaylen Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds and six assists. LeBron James added 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, and Joel Embiid had 13 points and 11 rebounds. For New York, Jalen Brunson scored 21, Karl-Anthony Towns had 19 points and 12 rebounds, and Andre Drummond grabbed 14 rebounds.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia is 1-0 and the East's No. 2 seed, while New York is 0-1 and 14th in the East.

headlines.title: Pistons beat Celtics 121–113 as George scores 38
headlines.summary: Paul George scored 38 with seven threes, five rebounds and five steals, but Boston lost 121–113 to Detroit. Cade Cunningham had 22 points and eight assists, and Jalen Duren added 22 points and nine rebounds. Duncan Robinson hit five threes for 21 points. Derrick White had eight assists for the Celtics, and Payton Pritchard scored 17.
headlines.whyItMatters: Detroit is 1-0 and the East's No. 1 seed, while Boston is 0-1 and 15th in the conference.

contextCard.title: How the NBA second apron works
contextCard.body: The second apron is the highest salary threshold in the NBA's luxury tax system. Teams above it face tighter trade rules, including not being able to take back more salary than they send out. That's why the Warriors' options for Kristaps Porzingis are limited.
